title: 35mm projector gate weave, splice and changeover cue
blurb: Projects a live editable screenplay and clapperboard card through one ElementGL WebGL 2 canvas with 24 fps stepped gate weave, Kodak red-orange halation, film grain, dust scratches, a splice jump and a top-right reel changeover cue.
question: Can one ElementGL WebGL 2 canvas emulate a real 35mm cinema projector gate over a live editable screenplay card with 24 fps stepped weave, red-orange emulsion halation, dust scratches, a film splice jump and a top-right changeover cue?
result: Measured in headless Chrome 160 Canary (2026-11-27, 412 px @ 2.625 DPR, SwiftShader): 6/6 live checks pass. One ElementGL WebGL 2 canvas uploads #reel-card via texElementSubImage2D() with UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL, holds 24 fps stepped gate weave identical within each 1/24 s slot, scatters red-orange halation around bright highlights, renders the top-right changeover cue and syncs hit testing with updateElementGeometry().
